claim.pdf_says: 14.9.15.2 General format:  FREE { data-name-1 } ...  - FREE is UNDERLINED (verified by rendering page 657 at 300 dpi and cropping the figure; the underline spans all four letters).
claim.why_it_matters: FREE is a required word; without the underline the figure formally reads as if FREE were an optional word (5.2.6.2). The braces and the trailing ellipsis (which correctly binds to the closing brace per 5.2.7) are transcribed correctly, so this is the only defect in the figure. The markdown already uses <u> in neighbouring formats (14.9.17.2, 14.9.18.2), so the loss is local.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed. (1) PDF: rendered page 657 (printed page 627) at 300 dpi and cropped the general-format line to a 3x upscale (E:/Temp/specrecon/v657/crop_free.png). The printed glyphs are 'FREE { data-name-1 } ...' with a solid horizontal rule running continuously beneath F-R-E-E and terminating before the opening brace. The underline is unmistakable and is not a scan artifact - it is a clean, full-width rule at baseline offset, and no other token on the line carries one. (2) Markdown: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27165 reads 'FREE { data-name-1 } ...' as plain text with no <u> markup, no bold, and no compensating prose. The surrounding lines 27162-27166 contain only the section anchor and heading, so the marker is not reflowed onto an adjacent line and is not present in any alternative form. (3) It is not mere formatting. The transcription's own text is dispositive: section 5.2.2 Keywords (line 2631) - 'They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword'; section 5.2.3 Optional words (line 2644) - 'They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity'. Underlining is therefore load-bearing notation, and its loss converts the statement verb FREE from a required keyword into an omissible optional word, making the bare '{ data-name-1 } ...' read as a legal FREE statement. That is a change of meaning, not typography. (4) The transcription has two established conventions for preserving this information - inline <u> markup (156 spans, e.g. '<u>GO</u> TO procedure-name-1' at 14.9.17.2, line 27291) and a 'Figure notes (...)' blockquote naming the underlined words (used for fenced diagrams, e.g. line 4874, which records that SOURCE/FIXED/FREE are underlined in the SOURCE FORMAT directive). Neither is applied at 14.9.15.2, so this is a real omission against the file's own conventions rather than a deliberate uniform policy. The rest of the figure - plain braces, single operand, trailing ellipsis binding to the closing brace per 5.2.7 - is transcribed correctly, as claimed.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, but the claim is inaccurate in three respects and its severity label is arguable. (a) Line number: the format line is 27165, not 27162; 27162 is the '' anchor. (b) Wrong citation: the required-versus-optional distinction is governed by 5.2.2 (Keywords: uppercase and underlined = required) and 5.2.3 (Optional words: uppercase and not underlined), NOT by 5.2.6.2, which is 'Brackets'. The claim's other citation, 5.2.7 for the ellipsis, is correct. (c) 'The loss is local' is false, and one of its two supporting examples is wrong: 14.9.17.2 does use ('GO TO procedure-name-1'), but 14.9.18.2 (GOBACK, line 27330) is a fenced block with no and no figure note. A survey of the whole file shows underline loss is systemic, not local: of 322 'General format' headings, only 74 have any in the body; restricting to the fairest comparison class - inline (non-fenced) formats, the same style as 14.9.15.2 - 71 carry and 79 do not. Page 657 is one instance of a document-wide transcription weakness, so the remediation should be a sweep over unfenced general formats rather than a one-line patch. Corrected finding: at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27165 the required-word underline printed on FREE in the PDF is absent, and should be restored as 'FREE { data-name-1 } ...' to match the file's existing convention. Severity note: the figure's structure (braces, operand, ellipsis binding) is intact; what is lost is a required-word marker, so this is more precisely a notation/markup loss than a structural one - though it does change the formal reading of the format.
